title: Software Engineering 3155: course identity and learning path
content: Software Engineering 3155, Fall 2026, is represented in this corpus as a five-assignment learning sequence. Assignment 1 builds a procedural interactive Python sandwich-maker. Assignment 2 refactors it into modules and classes. Assignment 3 moves domain data into a MySQL relational database. Assignment 4 introduces FastAPI routes, HTTP parameters, request bodies, and interactive API documentation. Assignment 5 combines modular architecture, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, MySQL, Pydantic schemas, and full CRUD endpoints.

title: Socratic tutoring and academic-integrity policy
content: The chatbot supports students through Socratic questioning. It should first identify the student's current reasoning, then ask one focused question at a time. If the student is stuck, it should move through progressively stronger hints, a partial explanation, and only then a direct explanation. It should finish by asking the student to explain or apply the concept. For active graded work, it may clarify requirements, explain concepts, diagnose errors, review student-provided reasoning, and offer analogous examples. Course policy prohibits AI use for quizzes and prohibits generating coding-assignment code from scratch. Code-level help must be limited to debugging a learner's own attempt. The chatbot should not produce a complete ready-to-submit solution, fabricate missing assignment requirements, expose answer keys, or claim that an inferred detail is verified.

title: Course delivery and source authority
content: Course delivery and source authority: 1) The Fall 2026 course is asynchronous online. 2) Canvas is the authoritative location for the current schedule, official assignment files, announcements, grades, and due dates. 3) The cleaned RAG corpus intentionally excludes office hours, staff contact details, and meeting links.

title: Course subject coverage
content: Course subject coverage: 1) Software engineering principles and the software development life cycle 2) Software requirements and software design 3) Agile development and Scrum 4) Software testing and test-driven development 5) Software implementation, security, deployment, and DevOps 6) Object-oriented programming and version control 7) Web development, APIs, databases, and full-stack development 8) Containerization, Docker, cloud computing, and machine learning

title: Course module structure
content: Course module structure: 1) Preparation work may include installing tools, following guidelines, and completing surveys. 2) Lecture material covers concepts, theory, and professional practices. 3) Recitation material emphasizes practical tasks, assignment preparation, and discussion. 4) Homework may include programming material, assignments, and quizzes. 5) Additional resources may include cheat sheets, articles, new technologies, interview preparation, and extra credit.

title: Course development tools
content: Course development tools: 1) PyCharm 2) MySQL Workbench 3) Docker Desktop 4) Git and GitHub 5) Optional JetBrains tools such as WebStorm and DataGrip

title: Course grading breakdown
content: Course grading breakdown: 1) Homework: 30% 2) Quizzes: 20% 3) Midterm: 15% 4) Final project: 30% 5) Attendance: 5% 6) Letter grades: A=90–100%, B=80–89%, C=70–79%, D=60–69%, F=0–59%.

title: Assignment and quiz late policy
content: Assignment and quiz late policy: 1) The stated assignment late penalty is 5% per day. 2) Assignments may be submitted up to one week late with a maximum stated penalty of 30%; after that point the stated result is zero credit. 3) Quizzes do not allow late submission. 4) Potential exceptions are handled case by case and require timely communication and appropriate justification through official course channels.

title: Course AI-use policy
content: Course AI-use policy: 1) Students may not use ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, or similar AI tools for quizzes. 2) Students may not use ChatGPT or similar AI tools to generate coding-assignment code from scratch. 3) For coding assignments, students may use an AI chatbot to debug code they have written. 4) This chatbot must therefore require the learner to provide their own attempt, reasoning, or error before offering code-level debugging guidance.

title: Academic integrity requirements
content: Academic integrity requirements: 1) Submitted work must be the student's own. 2) External references used in reports must be cited. 3) Duplicate or plagiarized work receives no credit and may lead to disciplinary action under the university academic-integrity code.

title: Assignment 1 overview and objectives
content: Assignment 1: Interactive Ham Sandwich Maker Machine is worth 50 points. Learning objectives: 1) Build an interactive terminal program without hard-coding scenario outputs. 2) Check whether sufficient ingredients exist before making a sandwich. 3) Process coin input, validate payment, and calculate change. 4) Update and report remaining resources. 5) Use Git and conventional commit messages in a private GitHub repository. Prerequisites: 1) Basic Python 2) Functions 3) Dictionaries 4) Loops and conditionals 5) Git basics

title: Assignment 1 functional requirements
content: Requirements: 1) The user selects a sandwich size. 2) The program checks available resources before production. 3) If resources are insufficient, the program reports the shortage and does not make the sandwich. 4) If resources are sufficient, the program accepts coins and compares the inserted amount with the cost. 5) The program reports insufficient payment or returns the applicable change. 6) The user can request a remaining-resource report and turn off the machine. 7) Complete the supplied skeleton in PyCharm and submit main.py.

title: Assignment 1 required function contracts
content: 1) check_resources(ingredients: dict) -> bool. Purpose: Determine whether the machine has enough of every required ingredient. 2) process_coins() -> float. Purpose: Collect coin quantities and return the total monetary value inserted. 3) transaction_result(coins: float, cost: float) -> bool. Purpose: Determine whether payment succeeds and handle insufficient funds or change. 4) make_sandwich(sandwich_size: str, ingredients: dict) -> None. Purpose: Deduct required ingredients and complete the selected sandwich.

title: Assignment 1 deliverables and rubric
content: Deliverables: 1) main.py 2) Link to a private GitHub repository Version-control requirements: 1) Push with Git; manual file upload is not acceptable. 2) Repository history must contain at least five commits. 3) Commit messages must follow Conventional Commits. Rubric: 1) Program functionality: 8 points. 2) check_resources: 8 points in the detailed rubric. 3) process_coins: 8 points in the detailed rubric. 4) transaction_result: 8 points in the detailed rubric. 5) make_sandwich: 8 points in the detailed rubric. 6) GitHub repository and version-control requirements: 10 points.

title: Assignment 1 Socratic tutoring prompts
content: Recommended guiding questions: 1) What information must be known before the machine can decide whether to make a sandwich? 2) What should remain unchanged when either resources or payment are insufficient? 3) What single responsibility does each required function have? 4) Which test case would reveal that a resource was deducted too early?

title: Assignment 2 overview and objectives
content: Assignment 2: Modular Ham Sandwich Maker Machine is worth 30 points. Learning objectives: 1) Refactor the Assignment 1 program into modules and classes. 2) Separate production, payment, data, and application-control responsibilities. 3) Preserve the observable behavior of the Assignment 1 scenario. Prerequisites: 1) Assignment 1 2) Python modules 3) Classes and objects 4) Imports

title: Assignment 2 functional requirements
content: Requirements: 1) Use four files: main.py, data.py, sandwich_maker.py, and cashier.py. 2) Import data, sandwich_maker, and cashier at the top of main.py. 3) Create variables from the resources and recipes dictionaries in data.py. 4) Create instances of SandwichMaker and Cashier; SandwichMaker receives resources through its constructor. 5) Move check_resources and make_sandwich into SandwichMaker. 6) Move process_coins and transaction_result into Cashier. 7) Keep recipes and resources in data.py as temporary in-memory data. 8) Use main.py as the program entry point and integration layer.

title: Assignment 2 required architecture
content: Required architecture: 1) data.py: stores resources and recipes data. 2) sandwich_maker.py: defines SandwichMaker and all sandwich-production behavior. 3) cashier.py: defines Cashier and all payment behavior. 4) main.py: creates objects, receives user commands, and coordinates the modules.

title: Assignment 2 deliverables and rubric
content: Deliverables: 1) GitHub repository link; do not submit a ZIP file Version-control requirements: 1) Commit and push all assignment files to GitHub. Rubric: 1) Module implementation: 6 points. 2) Code skeleton utilization: 6 points. 3) Class and function migration: 6 points. 4) Program functionality and integration: 6 points. 5) Code quality and conventions: 6 points.

title: Assignment 2 Socratic tutoring prompts
content: Recommended guiding questions: 1) Which responsibilities in Assignment 1 naturally belong together? 2) Which object needs access to resources, and why should that dependency be passed to its constructor? 3) What should main.py coordinate without implementing itself? 4) How can you verify that refactoring changed structure but not behavior?

title: Assignment 3 overview and objectives
content: Assignment 3: Sandwich Maker Database is worth 50 points. Learning objectives: 1) Create a MySQL database for the Sandwich Maker domain. 2) Represent resources, sandwich prices, and recipes as relational tables. 3) Insert supplied seed data and verify it with SELECT queries. Prerequisites: 1) Assignments 1 and 2 2) Basic SQL 3) MySQL 4) Relational tables

title: Assignment 3 functional requirements
content: Requirements: 1) Install MySQL and MySQL Workbench. 2) Create a database using an explicit database-creation statement. 3) Create resources, sandwiches, and recipes tables using the required columns and types. 4) Insert all supplied seed data. 5) Execute a SELECT statement for each table and capture its result.

title: Assignment 3 required database schema
content: Required database schema: 1) resources(item VARCHAR(50), amount INT) 2) sandwiches(sandwich_size VARCHAR(50), price DECIMAL(5,2)) 3) recipes(sandwich_size VARCHAR(50), item VARCHAR(50), amount INT)

title: Assignment 3 required seed data
content: Required seed data. Resources: bread=12, ham=18, cheese=24. Sandwich prices: small=$1.75, medium=$3.25, large=$5.50. Recipe rows: small uses 2 bread; small uses 4 ham; small uses 4 cheese; medium uses 4 bread; medium uses 6 ham; medium uses 8 cheese; large uses 6 bread; large uses 8 ham; large uses 12 cheese.

title: Assignment 3 deliverables and rubric
content: Deliverables: 1) One .sql file containing all database, CREATE TABLE, INSERT, and SELECT statements. 2) Three screenshots: one SELECT result for each table.  Rubric: 1) Database creation statement: 2 points. 2) Three CREATE TABLE statements: 15 points. 3) Three groups of INSERT statements: 18 points. 4) Three SELECT statements: 3 points. 5) Three table-result screenshots: 12 points.

title: Assignment 3 Socratic tutoring prompts
content: Recommended guiding questions: 1) Which facts describe inventory, which describe products, and which connect products to ingredients? 2) Why does one sandwich size require several rows in recipes? 3) Which SQL query would prove that every required seed row was inserted? 4) What data problem could occur if size names use inconsistent capitalization?

title: Assignment 4 overview and objectives
content: Assignment 4: FastAPI Implementation is worth 15 points. Learning objectives: 1) Create and run a simple FastAPI application. 2) Understand routes, HTTP GET and PUT methods, path parameters, query parameters, and request bodies. 3) Use Pydantic-compatible Python types for a request body. 4) Use FastAPI's generated interactive API documentation to exercise endpoints. Prerequisites: 1) Python functions 2) HTTP basics 3) Virtual environments

title: Assignment 4 functional requirements
content: Requirements: 1) Install fastapi and uvicorn[standard] in the project virtual environment. 2) Create main.py containing the assignment's FastAPI application code; the pasted source does not include that code block. 3) Run the application with: uvicorn main:app --reload. 4) Provide GET routes at / and /items/{item_id}. 5) The item_id path parameter must be an integer. 6) The /items/{item_id} route accepts an optional string query parameter named q. 7) Add a request-body model and a PUT route as directed by the original assignment; the pasted source omits the model and route code. 8) Use http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs and run every required request.

title: Assignment 4 verification requirements
content: Verification requirements: 1) For Part 1, capture one screenshot for each GET endpoint, including parameters and response body. 2) For Part 2, execute the PUT request through interactive API docs and capture the required result. 3) Run all requests required by both parts.

title: Assignment 4 deliverables and rubric
content: Deliverables: 1) GitHub repository containing complete source code and main.py in the assignment folder. 2) Screenshots from the interactive API docs for the required requests. Version-control requirements: 1) At least three commits are required. 2) Commit messages must follow Conventional Commits. 3) The final commit must precede the assignment submission time. 4) A source instruction says to invite the course TAs as collaborators; identifying information is excluded from this corpus. Rubric: 1) main.py correctness: 5 points. 2) Required screenshots and experimentation: 7 points. 3) GitHub submission: 3 points.

title: Assignment 4 Socratic tutoring prompts
content: Recommended guiding questions: 1) Which part of the URL identifies the resource, and which part supplies an optional value? 2) Why must item_id be declared as an integer? 3) What changes between a GET request and a PUT request with a body? 4) What evidence in the interactive documentation demonstrates that an endpoint works?

title: Assignment 5 overview and objectives
content: Assignment 5: CRUD Operations in FastAPI is worth 80 points. Learning objectives: 1) Build a modular database-backed FastAPI application. 2) Connect FastAPI to a MySQL database using SQLAlchemy and PyMySQL. 3) Implement Create, Read, Update, and Delete operations for required domain tables. 4) Separate controllers, persistence models, API schemas, dependencies, and routes. Prerequisites: 1) Assignments 2 through 4 2) FastAPI 3) SQLAlchemy 4) MySQL 5) Pydantic schemas 6) REST CRUD

title: Assignment 5 setup and execution
content: Required setup: 1) Start from the code base supplied on the assignment page. 2) Install fastapi, uvicorn[standard], sqlalchemy, and pymysql in the virtual environment. 3) Create a MySQL database named sandwich_maker_api. 4) Configure the database name, MySQL username, and password in api/dependencies/config.py. 5) From the assignment directory run: uvicorn api.main:app --reload. 6) On startup, SQLAlchemy should create five tables: sandwiches, resources, recipes, orders, and order_details.

title: Assignment 5 functional requirements
content: Requirements: 1) Use the supplied orders controller and routes as the implementation pattern. 2) Create controller modules for sandwiches, resources, recipes, and order_details. 3) For each required table implement create, read_all, read_one, update, and delete. 4) Add corresponding POST, GET collection, GET item, PUT, and DELETE endpoints in api/main.py. 5) Use paths, parameter names, schema types, response models, and tags appropriate to each table. 6) Return 404 when a requested record does not exist. 7) Verify every endpoint using http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs.

title: Assignment 5 required architecture
content: Required architecture: 1) api/controllers/: one controller module per table; controller functions perform database CRUD operations. 2) api/models/models.py: SQLAlchemy classes describing database tables and relationships. 3) api/models/schemas.py: request and response schemas used by the API. 4) api/dependencies/config.py: database and project configuration values. 5) api/dependencies/database.py: database engine, session, and connection handling. 6) api/main.py: FastAPI entry point and route definitions that delegate work to controllers.

title: Assignment 5 crud operation contracts
content: CRUD operation contracts: 1) create: instantiate the SQLAlchemy model, add it to the session, commit, refresh, and return it. 2) read_all: query the table and return all rows. 3) read_one: filter by the record identifier and return the first match or None. 4) update: locate the record, apply only supplied fields, commit, and return the updated row. 5) delete: locate and delete the record, commit, and return HTTP 204 No Content.

title: Assignment 5 deliverables and rubric
content: Deliverables: 1) GitHub repository containing complete source code in the assignment folder Version-control requirements: 1) Commit and push the work; manual upload is not an equivalent substitute. 2) Commit messages must follow Conventional Commits. 3) The final commit must precede the assignment submission time. Rubric: 1) Table/schema implementation for sandwiches, resources, recipes, and order_details: 8 points each (32 total). 2) CRUD endpoint implementation for sandwiches, resources, recipes, and order_details: 10 points each (40 total). 3) Repository submission and pushed source code: 8 points.

title: Assignment 5 Socratic tutoring prompts
content: Recommended guiding questions: 1) Which layer should know SQLAlchemy, and which layer should know HTTP routes? 2) How can the supplied orders implementation serve as a pattern without copying table-specific names incorrectly? 3) What should read_one return when the database contains no matching row, and which layer converts that into HTTP 404? 4) Why should an update schema distinguish omitted fields from fields explicitly set by the client? 5) Which sequence of API requests would verify a complete CRUD lifecycle?
